headline: Occupancy strength lifts NOI; merger clouds EPS outlook
summary_short: Equity Residential's Q2 FY2026 diluted EPS of $0.30 fell 40.0% y/y on lower property-sale gains, even as FFO per share rose 2.0% y/y to $1.00 and same-store NOI grew 1.4% on occupancy-led demand.
summary_long: Diluted EPS of $0.30 fell 40.0% y/y (up 25.0% q/q) on lower property-sale gains versus Q2 2025. Operating trends were firmer: revenue of $785.0M grew 0.7% q/q / 2.1% y/y, same-store revenue rose 1.9% y/y on strong occupancy (96.2%) and renewal-rate achievement, same-store NOI grew 1.4% y/y, and FFO/NFFO per share rose 2.0%/3.0% y/y to $1.00/$1.02. FY2026 same-store revenue and NOI guidance were raised (revenue to 2.1%-2.7%; NOI to 1.5%-2.1%) on San Francisco momentum and better bad debt, with expense guidance held at 3.0%-4.0%. EPS, FFO and NFFO per-share guidance were withdrawn given the pending AvalonBay merger. The quarter included two dispositions (515 units, ~$164.0M).

drivers.explanation: Release states the y/y decline is "due primarily to lower property sale gains" versus Q2 2025, plus other smaller FFO-reconciliation items.
Revenue growth was "driven by strong Physical Occupancy and better than anticipated Renewal Rate Achieved"; expenses grew faster than revenue, moderating NOI growth to 1.4%.
Guidance raise attributed to a solid demand environment, with "occupancy and resident retention that remain at historically high levels" plus a supportive job market and declining new supply.
